text: I. Professional OverviewProject management is an interdisciplinary subject that takes systematic thinking and structured methods as its core, integrates knowledge from multiple disciplines such as management, economics, law, and engineering technology, and conducts full life cycle control for one-off and unique projects (such as software development, engineering construction, event planning, etc.). Its core objective is to ensure the efficient delivery of the project under constraints such as scope, time, cost and quality through scientific planning, organization, coordination and control, while balancing the demands of all relevant parties. This major is not only applicable to traditional infrastructure, IT, and manufacturing, but also widely penetrates into emerging fields such as the Internet, cultural and creative industries, and healthcare. It is a key management tool for modern enterprises to implement their strategies.Ii. Training ObjectivesCultivate compound management talents with the ability to manage the entire project process, cross-domain coordination and risk prediction. Students need to master the standard methodologies for Project initiation, planning, execution, monitoring and closure (such as PMBOK, PRINCE2), be familiar with project management tools (such as MS Project, Jira), and be able to serve as project managers, project coordinators or strategic managers in industries such as technology research and development, engineering construction, Internet products, and financial investment. Promote the full-cycle management of complex projects from planning to implementation, serving the strategic goals of enterprises and the demands of major social projects.
